cards.front: What should you know about business exam tips?
cards.back: When discussing technology's impact, use the CED framework: Cost (investment vs savings), Efficiency (productivity gains), Disruption (effects on workers, customers, competitors). Always consider short-term costs versus long-term benefits.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Technology always benefits businesses because it reduces costs. Correct: Technology can increase costs initially (equipment, training, maintenance) and may alienate customers who prefer personal service. cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Technology in Business with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.

cards.front: Understanding Technology in Business in Business Context
cards.back: Technology in Business is a key topic in GCSE Business Studies that affects how businesses operate in the UK economy. Understanding this concept requires knowledge of both theoretical principles and real-world application. The AQA specification requires you to explain, analyse and evaluate business concepts using appropriate terminology, and apply them to real business scenarios using UK examples.

cards.front: Applying Technology in Business to UK Business Examples
cards.back: For technology in business, applying theory to practice means using real UK business examples to illustrate your understanding. Small businesses face different challenges from large corporations when dealing with technology in business. Consider how factors like business size, ownership structure, industry sector and market position affect the impact of technology in business on a business.

cards.front: Exam Technique for Technology in Business Questions
cards.back: GCSE Business exam questions about technology in business range from 1-mark definition questions to 12-mark evaluation questions.
